### [server.py](file:///c%3A/.Repo/Intellicap/test/server.py)

To use `server.py` to:
1. Start the Flask app (entry point: `run.py`) locally.
2. Start the Cloudflare tunnel using `subprocess.Popen(["cloudflared", "tunnel", "run", "flask"])`.

Here's a concise implementation:

````python
import subprocess
import sys
import time

# Start the Flask app (run.py)
flask_proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "c:\\.Repo\\Intellicap\\run.py"])

# Wait a bit to ensure Flask is up (adjust as needed)
time.sleep(3)

# Start the cloudflared tunnel
cloudflared_proc = subprocess.Popen(["cloudflared", "tunnel", "run", "flask"])

try:
    # Wait for both processes
    flask_proc.wait()
    cloudflared_proc.wait()
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    flask_proc.terminate()
    cloudflared_proc.terminate()
````

**Notes:**
- Adjust the path to `run.py` if needed.
- This script will terminate both processes on Ctrl+C.
- You may want to add more robust error handling or logging as needed.

### [server.bat](file:///c%3A/.Repo/Intellicap/test/server.bat)

Create a Windows batch file that:
- Self-elevates to admin if not already running as admin.
- Clears the terminal.
- Starts the Flask app.
- Waits a few seconds.
- Starts the Cloudflared tunnel.

Below is a concise batch file that accomplishes this. Place it in the same directory as your Python script or adjust paths as needed.

````batch
:: filepath: c:\.Repo\Intellicap\test\server.bat
@echo off
:: Self-elevate to admin
:: (If not running as admin, relaunch self as admin)
net session >nul 2>&1
if %errorLevel% neq 0 (
    powershell -Command "Start-Process '%~f0' -Verb RunAs"
    exit /b
)

:: Clear the terminal
cls

:: Start Flask app (adjust path as needed)
start "" "%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe" /k "python C:\.Repo\Intellicap\core\flask\run.py"

:: Wait a few seconds for Flask to start
timeout /t 3 /nobreak >nul

:: Start cloudflared tunnel
start "" "%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe" /k "cloudflared tunnel run flask"

:: Optional: Keep window open
pause
````

**Notes:**
- This script will open two new command windows: one for Flask, one for Cloudflared.
- Adjust the Python and script paths as needed.
- The self-elevation block uses PowerShell to relaunch the batch file as admin if needed.
- `pause` at the end keeps the window open so you can see any output/errors. Remove if not needed.

_**User**_

How can we check to see if the user's browser has been set to darkmode or not

---

_**Assistant**_

You can check if the user's browser is set to dark mode using the CSS media query `prefers-color-scheme: dark` or with JavaScript.

**Example (JavaScript):**

````javascript
// Check if browser prefers dark mode
if (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches) {
    // Dark mode is enabled
    console.log("Dark mode is enabled");
} else {
    // Light mode is enabled
    console.log("Light mode is enabled");
}
````

**Example (CSS):**

````css
/* ...existing code... */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    body {
        background-color: #222;
        color: #eee;
    }
    /* Add more dark mode styles here */
}
/* ...existing code... */
````

You can use either or both approaches depending on your needs.

### [base.html](file:///c%3A/.Repo/Intellicap/core/flask/templates/main/base.html)

To properly link your CSS, use Flask's `url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css')` in a `<link>` tag inside the `<head>` block.  
Make sure your `base.html` includes this line:

````html
<!-- ...existing code... -->
    <link href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css') }}" rel="stylesheet">
<!-- ...existing code... -->
````

**Summary:**  
- Place the above line in the `<head>` section of `base.html`.
- All templates extending `base.html` will now use your CSS.  
- Remove any incorrect or hardcoded CSS links from your other templates.

attaching the css automatically changes the background color, why

_**Assistant**_

The background color changes automatically when you attach your CSS because your CSS file contains rules that set the background color for the `body` (and possibly other elements). For example, you have:

```css
body {
    background-color: #fff;
    color: #000;
}
```

and in your previous versions, you had:

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    html, body {
        background-color: #ff0000 !important;
        color: #eee !important;
    }
}
```

When your CSS is loaded after Bootstrap, these rules override Bootstrap's defaults and set the background color accordingly. If you want to avoid changing the background color, simply remove or comment out these background-color rules from your CSS.

**Summary of what happens:**
- Your CSS is loaded after Bootstrap.
- Any `background-color` rule in your CSS will override Bootstrap's background color for the same selector.
- That's why attaching your CSS changes the background color.

When you link your own (even empty) CSS file after Bootstrap, the browser may re-calculate styles, but unless your CSS explicitly sets a background, it should not override Bootstrap's default.

**Possible reasons you still see a color change:**
- **Browser cache:** Your browser may be caching an older version of your CSS file that did set a background color. Try a hard refresh (Ctrl+F5) or clear your cache.

- **Bootstrap dark mode:** If your OS/browser is in dark mode, Bootstrap 5+ will automatically apply a dark background to `<body>`.

### [landing.html](file:///c%3A/.Repo/Intellicap/core/flask/templates/main/landing.html)

You have a `<body>` tag inside your `landing.html`, but your `base.html` already defines the `<body>`.  
This causes **nested `<body>` tags**, which can break CSS inheritance and cause browsers to render backgrounds incorrectly (often gray).

**Solution:**  
Remove the `<body>` tags from `landing.html`. Only use `{% block content %}`.

````html
{% extends "main/base.html" %}

{% block content %}
<!-- Your landing page content goes here -->
{% endblock %}
````

**Summary:**  
- Never put `<body>` in a template that extends a base template with its own `<body>`.
- Let `base.html` control the HTML structure.  
- This will fix the background color issue.

_**Assistant**_

You are seeing old CSS rules in the browser because your browser is **caching** the previous version of `main_page.css`. Even though you updated the file, the browser is still using the cached version.

**How to fix:**

1. **Hard Refresh:**  
   Press `Ctrl+F5` (Windows) or `Cmd+Shift+R` (Mac) to force the browser to reload all resources, bypassing the cache.

2. **Clear Cache:**  
   Go to your browser settings and clear the cache for your site.

3. **Cache Busting:**  
   Change the link to your CSS in your HTML to include a query string, e.g.:
   ```html
   <link href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css') }}?v=2" rel="stylesheet">
   ```
   This will force the browser to fetch the latest version.

4. **DevTools Disable Cache:**  
   Open DevTools (F12), go to the "Network" tab, and check "Disable cache" (while DevTools is open).

---

**Summary:**  
Your file on disk is correct, but the browser is using an old cached version. Hard refresh or use cache busting to see your latest changes.

_**Assistant**_

If you are seeing old CSS on new devices, it means your server is serving an outdated version of `main_page.css`. This is not a browser cache issue, but a **server-side cache or file mismatch**.

**Possible causes and solutions:**

1. **Wrong File Location:**  
   Make sure you are editing the correct file:
   ```
   c:\.Repo\Intellicap\core\flask\static\css\main_page.css
   ```
   and that Flask is serving static files from this directory.

2. **Flask Static Folder Configuration:**  
   Ensure your Flask app is configured to serve static files from `core/flask/static`.  
   By default, Flask serves from `static` in the app root. If your structure is different, set `static_folder` in your Flask app:
   ```python
   app = Flask(__name__, static_folder='static')
   ```
   or adjust as needed.

3. **File Not Updated on Server:**  
   If you are running the app in a container, virtual environment, or on a remote server, make sure the file is updated in the environment where Flask is running.

4. **Multiple CSS Files:**  
   Double-check that there are not multiple `main_page.css` files in different locations.  
   In DevTools, click the CSS file link and check the full path being served.

5. **Static File Versioning:**  
   Add a query string to your CSS link to force Flask to serve the latest file:
   ```html
   <link href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css') }}?v=999" rel="stylesheet">
   ```

6. **Flask Static File Caching:**  
   Flask may cache static files aggressively in production.  
   Try running Flask in debug mode, or set `SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT = 0` in your Flask config for development:
   ```python
   app.config['SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT'] = 0
   ```

---

**Summary:**  
- Confirm you are editing the correct file.
- Confirm Flask is serving the file you are editing.
- Use a query string version in your HTML link.
- Check Flask static file settings and caching.

If you follow these steps, you will see your latest CSS changes reflected everywhere.

4. **Your server is not actually deleting the file (e.g., running in a container or virtual environment with a different file system).**

**How to debug and fix:**

1. **Check the Network Tab:**
   - Open browser DevTools → Network tab.
   - Reload the page.
   - Click on `main_page.css` in the list.
   - Look at the "Response" tab. If it still shows CSS, the file is being served from somewhere.

2. **Check the File Path:**
   - In DevTools, check the full path of the CSS file being loaded.
   - Make sure it matches the file you deleted.

3. **Force Flask to Not Cache Static Files:**
   - In your Flask config, add:
     ```python
     app.config['SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT'] = 0
     ```
   - Restart your Flask server.

4. **Use a Query String to Bust Cache:**
   - In your HTML:
     ```html
     <link href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css') }}?v=999" rel="stylesheet">
     ```
   - This will force the browser to fetch the file again.

5. **Check for Other Copies:**
   - Search your entire project for `main_page.css` to ensure there are no duplicates.

6. **Restart Your Flask Server:**
   - Sometimes, the server needs to be restarted to reflect file changes.

   - Go to `http://127.0.0.1:5000/static/css/main_page.css` in your browser.
   - If you still see the file, it's being served from somewhere.

- The file is either cached, duplicated, or not actually deleted from the server's static directory.
- Use DevTools and direct file access to confirm what is being served.
- Restart Flask and clear all caches.

_**Assistant**_

If your browser DevTools shows the CSS is being loaded from `(index):12`, this means the CSS is being **injected directly into the HTML** (likely via a `<style>` tag in the `<head>`), not loaded from your static file.

**Why this happens:**
- Your `main_page.css` is not being found or loaded, so Flask (or Jinja) may be injecting an old or default style block.
- Or, you have a `<style>` block in your template that contains the CSS.

**How to fix:**

1. **Check your base.html and landing.html for `<style>` tags.**
   - Remove any inline `<style>` blocks that contain the old CSS.

2. **Check your `<link>` tag in base.html:**
   - Make sure it is:
     ```html
     <link href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/main_page.css') }}" rel="stylesheet">
     ```
   - Make sure there is **no** `<style>` tag with the same CSS.

3. **Ensure main_page.css is actually deleted from all static folders.**
   - Check for duplicate static folders or files.

4. **Restart your Flask server.**
   - Sometimes Flask needs a restart to update static file serving.

5. **Check for template inheritance issues.**
   - Make sure you are not extending a template that injects a `<style>` block.

---

**Summary:**  
- `(index):12` means the CSS is coming from a `<style>` tag in your HTML, not from your static file.
- Remove any inline `<style>` blocks from your templates.
- Ensure your `<link>` tag is correct and your static file is being served as expected.
- Restart Flask after changes.
